result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide concrete parking apron that lacks a dedicated, separated sidewalk. There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian-specific safety features, forcing pedestrians to share space with parked and moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of separated sidewalk
hazards.description: Pedestrians must navigate through a parking apron or walk on the roadway edge due to the absence of a protected walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and along the front of the commercial building

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks any painted markings to designate a safe crossing point for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area to the right of the building

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the concrete apron and the building's proximity to the road edge may block visibility between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the building and parking area near the side street

interventions.title: Construct a separated sidewalk
interventions.description: Install a raised, ADA-compliant sidewalk with a curb to provide physical separation between pedestrians and the parking/roadway area.

interventions.title: Mark high-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental-style pavement markings at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Install curb ramps
interventions.description: Provide sloped transitions at the intersection corners to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at an intersection adjacent to a commercial gas station. While a sidewalk is present on one side, it is not connected by marked crosswalks or supported by curb ramps, forcing pedestrians to navigate uncontrolled vehicle paths across a wide driveway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks or signs to alert drivers to pedestrians crossing at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and midground intersection area

hazards.name: Wide Commercial Driveway
hazards.description: The gas station has a very wide, continuous curb cut that increases the distance pedestrians are exposed to vehicles entering and exiting.
hazards.location_in_image: Right midground, entrance to the gas station

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or traffic signals are visible to regulate vehicle movement at the junction.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at the corners to provide accessible transitions to the roadway.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the gas station entrance using curbs or bollards to shorten pedestrian crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The intersection is a wide, multi-lane expanse that lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or dedicated pedestrian signals. The environment is heavily car-oriented, requiring pedestrians to traverse a significant distance without protection or clear right-of-way.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and foreground of the intersection

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway creates a long exposure time for pedestrians to conflicting vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Spanning the width of the roadway from left to right

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, meaning there is no dedicated phase or timing for people to cross safely.
hazards.location_in_image: On the traffic signal mast arms and poles

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style pavement markings to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The environment is highly car-centric and lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks, marked crosswalks, or ADA-compliant ramps. Pedestrians are forced to navigate unpaved shoulders and wide, unmarked roadway crossings, which significantly increases the risk of conflict with vehicles.

hazards.name: Absence of Sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians are forced to walk on the grass or the edge of the roadway, increasing the risk of being struck by vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left sides of the roadway throughout the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked locations for pedestrians to cross the wide roadway safely.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the center of the image.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from vehicular traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with signage to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Tighten the corner radii at driveways and intersections to slow turning vehicles and shorten crossing distances.
